editorial:
Dogman (2023) is a wild ride that mixes crime drama with a deep love story between a man and his dogs. You follow Douglas, a guy who survived a brutal childhood and found his only real family in a pack of loyal dogs. The movie bounces between his past trauma and his present life as a drag performer and dog trainer who gets pulled into the criminal underworld. It's strange, emotional, and sometimes shocking, but it keeps you watching because you genuinely care about Douglas and his furry friends. The tone shifts from dark to tender to action-packed, so you never quite know what's coming next.

Caleb Landry Jones gives a committed, intense performance that carries the whole film. The dog scenes are impressive and heartfelt, and the action moments hit hard when they arrive. On the downside, the story can feel messy and over-the-top, and some plot turns are hard to believe. If you enjoy character-driven crime stories with an emotional core, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final act, Douglas refuses to back down when criminals threaten him and his dogs. He unleashes his pack on the gang, turning the tables in a brutal showdown. Police arrive and arrest Douglas, but he finally feels at peace. His dogs are safe, he stood up for himself, and the cycle of abuse that defined his life is broken. The last shot shows him calm and content, finally free in spirit even behind bars.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven crime stories with an emotional core.
